name: Carolingian Empire

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1.1 million km2 for 752-840 (low); Wikipedia infobox 1.2 million km2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolingian_Empire); the world_800 polygon measures 1.19 million km2.

population.note: Seshat codes 20 million (disputed) and 15 million (expert, 811). Wikipedia gives 10-20 million (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolingian_Empire); the Medieval demography article puts Europe at 25-30 million under Charlemagne, about half in the empire (12-15 million).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Largest settlement 20,000-30,000 (Seshat, Rome); most "towns" were episcopal seats of a few thousand.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing element only: palace household troops (scara), vassi dominici in attendance and march garrisons (Saxon, Avar, Spanish and Breton marches). Lot (via https://www.medievalists.net/2026/03/size-armies-early-medieval-warfare/) held that even Charlemagne rarely assembled 5,000 men. audit 2026-10-30: date basis: a year without a general muster, so only the household element is active and campaign levies are trainedReserves (france-1415, dated to the Agincourt campaign, counts its assembled army instead).

trainedReserves.note: Werner (1968) estimated Charlemagne could raise 30,000-35,000 heavily armed horsemen and up to 100,000 lighter troops north of the Alps (high, via medievalists.net summary of the debate); the small-army school (Lot, Verbruggen) puts campaign armies at a few thousand. Mid between the schools. These are vassal and free-man obligations under the capitularies, callable for the annual May muster.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Household officials, engineers, carts and coastal guard crews ordered in 800-811.

mobilizationRatio.note: Werner's total (30,000-35,000 heavy horse + up to 100,000 lighter troops = ~135,000) over 15 million inhabitants = 0.9%. Low reflects the small-army school.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Scara and royal vassals with mail byrnie, lance, sword and shield, as required by the capitularies of 792-805.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Frankish swords and byrnies were export-banned (Capitulary of Thionville 805) as the best in the West.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: noble warriors trained from youth, no drill.

count.note: Educated guess. Garrison foot in the marches and royal estates.
Educated guess. Archers: the capitulary of Aachen 802-803 required each soldier to bring a bow.
Educated guess. Mounted scouts and frontier horsemen in the marches.
Educated guess. Stone throwers (petrariae) and rams used at Pavia (773-774) and in the Spanish March; built on site.
Educated guess. Coastal guard ships ordered after Charlemagne's inspection of the Channel coast in 800 and the Danube boat bridges of the Avar war; no standing navy.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Charlemagne ran annual campaigns with multi-column convergent operations (Avar war 791) and written mobilisation orders; no staff system.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: feudal host bound by personal oaths, held together by a strong king.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: thirty years of victories (Lombards 774, Saxons, Avars 796).

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: pattern-welded and early crucible swords, lance, bow; no crossbow or counterweight trebuchet.

armor.note: Anchor 3 (mail): the byrnie, scarce and expensive.

ships.note: Anchor 2 (oared war galleys) at best: coastal and river craft; no war fleet.

fortification.note: Anchor 2-3: Roman city walls, timber-and-earth burgs (Eresburg, Paderborn).

logistics.note: Anchor 3 (depot system): carts carrying three months of food ordered by the capitularies (letter to Abbot Fulrad, 806).

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID) UK 1000 = 1,151, France 1 CE = 956, Italy 1 CE = 1,407 (2011 int$); the 9th-century West was poorer than Roman Gaul or Italy and than England in 1000.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Service in kind by vassals; no monetised budget.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Estate crafts, swords and textiles.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Manorial agriculture with low yields.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Surviving Roman roads in Gaul, Italy and the Rhineland; none east of the Rhine.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Dorestad, Quentovic, Marseille, Arles, Ravenna area.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Frisian and Mediterranean coastal shipping.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.1-0.25 oxen and horses per inhabitant.

chokepoints: Great St Bernard and Mont Cenis passes

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar terrain and local supply; few fortified towns.

notes: Snapshot = December 800, Charlemagne's imperial coronation. Army size is the most disputed number of the early Middle Ages: Lot ("rarely 5,000"), Verbruggen and Delbrueck argue for small armies, Werner (30,000-35,000 heavy horse + up to 100,000 others) and Bernard Bachrach for large ones (summary at https://www.medievalists.net/2026/03/size-armies-early-medieval-warfare/; Bachrach, Charlemagne's Early Campaigns, 2013, builds on Werner). activePersonnel counts only the standing household and march garrisons; the vassal and free-man host is trainedReserves and mobilizable, per the feudal-host convention. Population convention: everything inside the empire including Lombard Italy and the Spanish March; papal Rome counted, tributary Slavs and Bretons not.
